items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Big Boy Goldie was not with the band and Fletcher Allen had been hired in his place.

ctx.x: Willie engaged Tommy Benford as a drummer. Also another trumpet player who had been in France for a long time who's name was Theordore Brock and a tenor man who was living in France for years named Bernard and was said to be the wealthiest Negro American musician in France. I never found out where Brock or Bernard were from in the States or who they have come to Europe with. I should have been a little more nosy than I was, but I never did ask other people many questions about themselves.

We opened the Coliseum in October with a French orchestra on another stand and there were about 30 dancing hostess's engaged for men who came alone which was run on the taxi dance plan, but we did not play like the New York dancing school bands had to play. Willie also raised my salary to one thousand francs a week which was quite a good salary in 1938. The band now had two tenors and two altos. Big Boy Goldie was not with the band and Fletcher Allen had been hired in his place.

Fletcher had worked with Freddie Taylor and left to go to India with the first group that Leon had taken to Bombay. Joe Hayman was still there. The other changes were Brock in the place of Jack Butler and Benford in the place of Ted Fields.
